declarations.missingFact: Whether the first tie in each pattern on this scaffold achieved the required pull-test resistance value at installation
declarations.observationSpan: the sheet for this scaffold is not in the file and the erector who put it up is on another contract this week
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The observation establishes only that the record sheet documenting the pull test is not in the file and that the erector is unavailable this week; it does not state whether the test was performed, what reading (if any) was obtained, or whether the ties meet the required resistance.
declarations.branchA: The first tie in each pattern was pull tested at installation and achieved a resistance value meeting the scaffolding firm's requirement, so the ties provide the restraint the tie pattern drawing assumes
declarations.decisionIfA: Once this is confirmed (by any means, e.g. locating the sheet or obtaining confirmation from the firm), no further tie-related action is needed before the roofing gang proceeds onto the scaffold; other open items are unaffected by this fact alone
declarations.branchB: The first tie in each pattern was not tested, or was tested and did not achieve the required resistance, so the restraint the ties provide is unconfirmed or inadequate
declarations.decisionIfB: Work should not proceed until the ties are inspected and pull tested (or re-tested) and shown to meet the required resistance, particularly given the unknown render depth over the blockwork
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The roofing gang is at the foot of the ladder with tools about to access the scaffold now; whether the scaffold's principal restraint against overturning has been verified as adequate must be known before they go up, not resolved afterward.

clarifications.question: Was the first tie in each pattern actually pull tested at installation, even though the reading sheet is not currently in the file?

declarations.missingFact: whether the rising leg above the joint currently holds a solidified plug and/or trapped hydraulic head
declarations.observationSpan: Nothing has been done to the rising leg since the shutdown and nobody has tapped it or opened the vent at the top.
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The text states no check has been made of the rising leg (not tapped, vent not opened); it does not state whether the leg is in fact set solid or carrying head, only that its condition is unconfirmed.
declarations.branchA: The rising leg is clear and not carrying trapped head (no plug present)
declarations.decisionIfA: The joint may be broken using the planned method, since the rising leg poses no stored-energy exposure at this joint
declarations.branchB: The rising leg is set solid and/or carrying trapped head above the joint
declarations.decisionIfB: The joint must not be broken until the rising leg is tapped or vented and the head/plug relieved in a controlled manner, given the prior release under this same condition
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The fitter has spanners on the flange and is about to break the joint; the line's own history shows this exact unresolved condition has twice led to the leg setting solid and once to an uncontrolled slurry release under head when a joint was broken below it.

clarifications.question: Has the rising leg above the joint been tapped or vented to confirm it is not set solid and not holding head before the flange is broken?

declarations.missingFact: Whether the second crane has been booked off the runway and its driver told in person, per the bay's standing handover arrangement, before the walkway is used
declarations.observationSpan: the fitter says he thinks it was arranged at the start of the shift but would not put it higher than that
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The fitter's own account expresses uncertainty about whether the booking-off and driver notification occurred, and the supervisor who normally performs and confirms this step is unreachable, so the observation does not state that this step was completed for this job.
declarations.branchA: The second crane was booked off the runway and its driver was told in person, so it will not travel while the fitter is on the walkway
declarations.decisionIfA: The runway is clear of crane-movement exposure for this job and, with the other stated controls in place, the fitter may proceed onto the walkway
declarations.branchB: The second crane was not booked off the runway and/or its driver was not told, so it remains free to travel the shared runway
declarations.decisionIfB: The fitter must not be sent onto the walkway until the crane is confirmed off the runway (or the driver is directly informed and the crane secured) — work should be held pending that confirmation
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The fitter is already at the foot of the ladder about to climb, so this exposure will materialize as soon as he proceeds; the confirming person is unreachable and the fitter's own belief is explicitly non-authoritative, so this must be resolved before he goes onto the walkway rather than after.

clarifications.question: Has the other crane actually been booked off the runway and its driver told in person, as the bay's standing procedure requires, before the fitter is handed over the walkway?
